Compare up to three products by price per unit to instantly see which pack or brand is the best deal.

Enter at least two products to compare.

Unit price = price ÷ quantity. Use the same quantity unit (g, ml, pieces) for every product.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the price and quantity for each product you want to compare.
  2. Quantities can be any unit (pieces, grams, ml) as long as you use the same unit across products.
  3. The tool divides price by quantity and flags the lowest unit price as the best deal.
  4. It also shows how much more expensive each other option is, in percent.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Do the quantities need to be in the same unit?

Yes. Compare grams with grams or pieces with pieces. Mixing units (e.g. 500g vs 1kg) still works only if you enter the raw numbers in the same base unit.

Why does the cheapest pack not always win?

Because unit price ignores pack size. A bigger pack usually has a lower price per unit, so it wins even though you pay more upfront.

How is the percentage difference calculated?

Each product's unit price is divided by the best unit price, minus one, expressed as a percent. A value of 25% means it costs 25% more per unit than the best deal.
